summary: Three measured rounds on Ascend 910B4 (all 36 workloads passing throughout): the seed scored geo_mean 0.825, and profiling plus target probes showed two distinct regimes — nine of twelve timing workloads are host-launch bound (1.65 us device task against a 13.2 us walltime) while the three large ones are bound by MTE transfer count, not bytes or program count. Rewriting the per-call host dispatch (module-bound Tensor methods, numel-keyed table, single-frame launcher call, still reading this call's address, dtype, contiguity and stream) raised geo_mean to 0.884 as the best round; the follow-up bf16 narrowing to fp16-width math did deliver its predicted device win (selu_-timing-7 83.3 -> 63.5 us, 0.710 -> 0.932) but the round scored 0.873 because the byte-identical fp16/fp32 small workloads and their references drifted +12% together, so it was reverted per the ledger. Key lesson: on this shared card a cross-round geo_mean at the ~12 us scale is noise-dominated — verify with retest or per-workload device durations, and note that fp32 large is pinned at BLOCK 8192 because every fp32-domain BLOCK 16384 form overflows UB.
